transcript: I was a lonely little girl, not the has-no-friends type of lonely, the lonely that has her ears glued to her bedroom door, listening to her parents break glass in the kitchen, their words sharper than the pieces shattered on the floor. I was the kind of lonely that built worlds in her head, imaginary places where love was gentle and voices never rose in anger, the kind of lonely that made her wonder why love always seemed to hurt. Even now, with years between me and that childhood, a part of me still presses her ear to the door, still flinches at the sound of breaking glass, still waits for the storm to pass, hoping the silence will mean peace. Because even when you grow up, a part of you stays, that lonely little girl, the one who learned too young that love could bruise just as easily as it could heal. She's still there, hiding in the quiet corners of my heart, clutching her dreams like fragile pieces of glass, afraid that even the gentlest touch could shatter them. And no matter how much I grow or how strong I become, I know I'll always carry her with me, the girl who learned to love from a distance, who learned to protect herself by staying small, yet still longs for the love she was never sure how to find. I think a part of me will always be a little lonely, that lonely little girl.
